'''Ōhara Sakurai''' (大原桜井) was a {{ill|Imperial Family of Japan|ja|皇族|zh|日本皇族|qid=Q11581068}}, {{ill|Nobility|ab|Аамсҭара|af|Adel|als|Adel|ar|نبل|ast|Nobleza|az|Zadəganlıq|ba|Дворянлыҡ|be|Знаць|be_x_old|Дваранства|bg|Аристокрация|bjn|Kasuma|br|Noblañs|bs|Plemstvo|ca|Noblesa|ckb|نەجیبزادەیی|cs|Šlechta|cv|Тăрăн|da|Adel|de|Adel|el|Ευγενείς|eo|Nobelaro|es|Nobleza|et|Aadel|eu|Noblezia|fa|نجیب‌زادگی|fi|Aateli|fr|Noblesse|frr|Aadel|fy|Eallju|ga|Uaisleacht|gan|貴族|gl|Nobreza|he|אצולה|hi|कुलीनवर्ग|hr|Plemstvo|hu|Nemesség|hy|Ազնվականություն|ia|Nobilitate|id|Bangsawan|ig|Onye isi|inh|Эздий|io|Nobeleso|is|Aðall|it|Nobiltà|ja|貴族|jv|Ningrat|ka|თავადაზნაურობა|ko|귀족|ku|Torinî|la|Nobilitas|lb|Adel|lmo|Nobiltà|lt|Diduomenė|lv|Dižciltīgie|min|Bangsawan|mk|Благородништво|mr|सामंतशाही|ms|Golongan bangsawan|myv|Мастачей|mzn|نوبرس|nds_nl|Adel|ne|भारदार परिवार|nl|Adel|nn|Adel|no|Adel|oc|Noblesa|pa|ਕੁਲੀਨਵਰਗ|pl|Szlachta|ps|اشرافیت / اشرافي خلک|pt|Nobreza|ro|Nobilime|ru|Дворянство|sh|Plemstvo|simple|Nobility|sk|Šľachta|sl|Plemstvo|sq|Fisnikëria|sr|Племство|sv|Adel|th|ชนชั้นขุนนาง|tl|Hadlika|tr|Asil|tt|Дворяннар|uk|Шляхта|uz|Dvoryanlar|vec|Nobiltà|vi|Giới quý tộc|wuu|贵族|za|Gveicuz|zh|貴族|zh_min_nan|Kùi-cho̍k|zh_yue|貴族|qid=Q134737|lt=aristocrat}}, and {{ill|waka poet|ja|歌人}} during the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}}. Initially known as '''Sakurai-Ō''' (桜井王), he adopted the name '''Ōhara Sakurai''' after his {{ill|Demotion to subject status|fa|شینسکی کوکا|ja|臣籍降下|ko|신적강하|zh|臣籍降下|zh_min_nan|Sîn-che̍k kàng-hā|qid=Q8193495}}, taking the surname {{ill|Q11433162|ja|大原氏|pt|Clã Ohara|qid=Q11433162}} (Ōhara no Mahito). He was a descendant of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|en|Emperor Bidatsu|qid=Q316637|lt=Emperor Bidatsu}}<ref>『{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}』Left Capital, Imperial Lineage</ref><ref name="o">"Onishiyama Daisōzu-den" in 『{{ill|Nihon Kōsōden Yōbunshō|ja|日本高僧伝要文抄}}』Vol. 3</ref>, and the son of {{ill|Kawachi-no-Mikoto|ja|河内王|qid=Q17209039}}. His official Rank was {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank}} and {{ill|Q11487787|ja|弾正尹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Danjon no in|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11487787}}.

== Biography ==

=== Early Career ===
In the 7th year of {{ill|Wadō (era)|en|Wadō (era)|qid=Q1373026|lt=Wadō}} (714), Sakurai was directly promoted to {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従五位下|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade}} from no Rank. In the 5th year of {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō}} (721), he was elevated to {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}}. That same year, when {{ill|Princess Inoe|en|Princess Inoe|qid=Q7244649|lt=Princess Inoe}} was designated as a {{ill|Saiō|en|Saiō|qid=Q19841349|lt=saiō}} and performed the {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/offering ceremony|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11445508}} at {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}, he served as a palanquin bearer along with {{ill|Tachibana no Moroe|en|Tachibana no Moroe|qid=Q3135863|lt=Prince Katsuragi}}.<ref>『{{ill|Seiji Yōryaku|ja|政事要略|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seiji Yōryaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11499054}}』Vol. 24</ref>

=== Under Emperor Shōmu ===
In the 1st year of {{ill|Jinki (era)|en|Jinki (era)|qid=Q1373210|lt=Shinki}} (724), shortly after {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|en|Emperor Shōmu|qid=Q349263|lt=Emperor Shōmu}}'s accession, Sakurai was promoted to {{ill|Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade|ja|正五位下|lt=Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade}}. By the 6th year of Shinki (729), he attained {{ill|Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|正五位上|lt=Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}}, and in the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}} (730), he reached {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従四位下|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}}. During this time, he served as {{ill|Chamberlain of Japan|ja|侍従|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chamberlain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2948088}} to Emperor Shōmu. Alongside his siblings, including {{ill|Takayasu Ohara|ja|大原高安|qid=Q17989661}} and {{ill|Prince Kadobe|ja|大原門部|qid=Q21015216|lt=Ōhara Kadohata}}, Sakurai was one of the "refined chamberlains" (風流侍従).<ref>『{{ill|Tōshi Kaden|en|Tōshi Kaden|qid=Q3020006|lt=Fujishi Kaden}}』 武智麻呂伝</ref>

In the 11th year of Tenpyō (739), Sakurai and his siblings, Kōan and Kadohata, were granted the surname {{ill|Ōhara clan|ja|大原真人}}, marking their demotion to commoner status. During his tenure as {{ill|Q104539334|ja|大蔵卿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkurakyō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q104539334}} in the 16th year of Tenpyō (744), he was assigned as the deputy administrator of {{ill|Kuni-kyō|en|Kuni-kyō|qid=Q1155335|lt=Kuni-kyō}} during Emperor Shōmu's visit to {{ill|Naniwa Palace|ja|難波宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naniwa Palace|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3608523}}.

=== Later Life ===
Later, Sakurai served as {{ill|Q11487787|ja|弾正尹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Danjon no in|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11487787}}. According to waka preserved in the {{ill|Man'yōshū|en|Man'yōshū|qid=Q834321|lt=Man'yōshū}},<ref name="m4478">『万葉集』巻20-4478</ref> he lived until at least the 8th year of {{ill|Tenpyō-shōhō|en|Tenpyō-shōhō|qid=Q1373169|lt=Tenpyō Shōhō}} (756) during {{ill|Empress Kōken|en|Empress Kōken|qid=Q232955|lt=Empress Kōken}}'s reign.<ref name="oz">Ozaki [2009: 10]</ref>

== Literary Contributions ==
As a poet, Sakurai's works are preserved in the Man'yōshū. These include a waka exchanged with Emperor Shōmu during his tenure as the governor of {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|en|Tōtōmi Province|qid=Q1048864|lt=Tōtōmi Province}} in the 5th year of Tenpyō (732)<ref name="m8">『万葉集』巻8-1614</ref> and a waka composed near the {{ill|Saho River|ja|佐保川}} around 756.<ref name="m4478" />

== Career Timeline ==
Details not explicitly noted are from the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|en|Shoku Nihongi|qid=Q611399|lt=Shoku Nihongi}}.
* [[:en:Wadō|Wadō]] 7 (714): Promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (direct promotion).
* {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō}} 5 (721): Promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade.
* {{ill|Shinki|en|Shinki|qid=Q15945968|lt=Shinki}} 1 (724): Promoted to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (February 22).
* Shinki 6 (729): Promoted to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade (March 4).
* {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}} 3 (730): Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (January 27).
* Date unknown: Appointed governor of Tōtōmi Province.<ref name="m8" />
* Tenpyō 11 (739): Granted the surname Ōhara no Mahito (April 3).
* Date unknown: Appointed Ōkurakyō.
* Tenpyō 16 (744): Appointed deputy administrator of Kuni-kyō (February 2).
* Date unknown: Appointed Danjon no in.<ref name="o" />
